note: Card 027. run1: first run (target rule without the revision rules), stopped at the gate. run2: revised rule (moves that end the way's condition refused; acts that do not turn the parent true marked for the episode), gate and main. run3: as run2 with the encoder's rows balanced by outcome. run4: counting decides the kinds, the network learns to recognise them; leave-one-out reported.

run1.note: Card 027, tools/card027/kinds.py; exact conditions and walking, kinds from pixels.
run1.run: timeout 1800 bin/prun python tools/card027/kinds.py --out runs/027_kinds.json (log runs/027kinds.out); 115 s; stopped after the gate

diagnosis.how: each failing layout of the exact-kinds arm replayed step by step (scratch trace, same code and layouts)

pattern_examples.12: picks up the other key that blocks the matching key, drops it back on the tile it came from (every floor tile is a target), repeats
pattern_examples.363: both keys pass the dependence test; walking toward the nearer key's spot turns left, the exact condition turns right; alternates

pattern_examples.56: switch on; the way 'toggle so the door can be opened' still applies (breaking the vase would clear the path), the switch passes the dependence test, the agent faces it and toggles it off; repeats
pattern_examples.71: the switch is the right tile but only one side works (acting from the other side leaves the door out of reach); walking toward the nearer side turns right, the exact condition turns left; alternates

diagnosis.root_cause: the target test asks whether the way's route depends on a thing (remove it and see), not whether acting on it from that spot would achieve the parent; the two differ for drop (a place), for a switch already on, and for which side to act from

diagnosis.how: the main arm replayed layout by layout with the run's learned codes (reproduces 0.994 and the random-move counts exactly); each random move classified by why no move was chosen
diagnosis.cause: the encoder gave the goal square the green closed door's code in both worlds; so the door-toggle way's kind includes the goal square, which is in every layout; the dependence test keeps it (removing the goal ends the route); it lies behind the closed door, so no move gets closer and the move is random
